name: Orion
description: The Hunter — three-star Belt is the most recognizable asterism in the night sky.

name: Ursa Major
description: Great Bear, containing the Big Dipper asterism. Pointer stars find Polaris.

name: Ursa Minor
description: Little Bear, Little Dipper. Polaris (the North Star) marks the bowl tip.

name: Cassiopeia
description: Distinctive W or M shape, circumpolar from mid-northern latitudes.

name: Cepheus
description: House-shaped circumpolar constellation next to Cassiopeia.

name: Draco
description: Long winding Dragon between the two Bears. Thuban was the pole star ~3000 BC.

name: Lyra
description: Small parallelogram anchored by Vega, brightest star of the Summer Triangle.

name: Cygnus
description: Northern Cross / Swan flying down the Milky Way. Deneb is the third Summer Triangle vertex.

name: Aquila
description: The Eagle. Altair completes the Summer Triangle with Vega and Deneb.

name: Boötes
description: Kite-shaped Herdsman. Arcturus is the brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere.

name: Virgo
description: Largest zodiacal constellation. Follow Arcturus's curve from the Big Dipper to find Spica.

name: Leo
description: The Lion — Sickle asterism (a backwards question mark) is the head and mane.

name: Scorpius
description: True scorpion shape with hooked tail. Antares, the red 'rival of Mars,' marks the heart.

name: Sagittarius
description: Teapot asterism aimed at the galactic center. Densest part of the Milky Way.

name: Taurus
description: The Bull — Hyades V-shape forms the face, Pleiades cluster sits on the shoulder.

name: Gemini
description: The Twins — bright pair Castor and Pollux mark the heads.

name: Cancer
description: Faint zodiac constellation. Hosts the Beehive Cluster (M44), naked-eye from dark sites.

name: Perseus
description: Hero standing between Cassiopeia and Taurus. Algol is a famous eclipsing binary.

name: Andromeda
description: Hosts M31, the Andromeda Galaxy — the most distant naked-eye object (2.5 Mly).

name: Pegasus
description: Great Square of Pegasus is the autumn signpost. Shares Alpheratz with Andromeda.

name: Auriga
description: The Charioteer — pentagonal shape near Taurus and Gemini. Capella is the sixth-brightest star.

name: Canis Major
description: Greater Dog — Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky, follows Orion across the south.

name: Canis Minor
description: Lesser Dog — Procyon completes the Winter Triangle with Sirius and Betelgeuse.

name: Crux
description: Southern Cross — smallest constellation, signpost for the south celestial pole.

name: Carina
description: The Keel — Canopus is the second-brightest star in the night sky. Hosts the Carina Nebula.
